verses.text: Jesus said to his followers, "Things that make people fall into sin are sure to come, but how terrible for the person through whom they come!
It would be better for them if a millstone were hung around their neck and they were thrown into the sea, than for them to cause one of these little ones to fall into sin.
Be careful. If your brother sins against you, tell him he is wrong. If he turns from it, forgive him.
If he sins against you seven times in a day, and seven times comes back and says, 'I am sorry,' you must forgive him."
The apostles said to the Lord, "Give us more faith."
The Lord said, "If you had faith as small as a mustard seed, you could say to this mulberry tree, 'Be pulled up by the roots and planted in the sea,' and it would obey you.
Suppose one of you has a servant who is ploughing or looking after sheep. When he comes in from the field, will you say to him, 'Come at once and sit down to eat'?
Will you not rather say, 'Prepare my supper, get yourself ready, and serve me while I eat and drink. After that you can eat and drink'?
Will you thank the servant because he did what he was told? I do not think so.
So you also, when you have done everything you were told to do, should say, 'We are servants who deserve nothing. We have only done our duty.'"
On the way to Jerusalem, Jesus travelled along the border between Samaria and Galilee.
As he entered a village, ten men with skin diseases met him. They stood at a distance
and called out, "Jesus, Master, have mercy on us!"
When he saw them, he said, "Go and show yourselves to the priests." And as they went, they were made clean.
One of them, when he saw that he was healed, came back, praising God with a loud voice.
He threw himself at Jesus's feet and thanked him. And he was a Samaritan.
Jesus asked, "Were not all ten made clean? Where are the other nine?
Was no one found to come back and give glory to God except this foreigner?"
Then he said to the man, "Get up and go. Your faith has healed you."
Once the Pharisees asked Jesus when the kingdom of God would come. He answered, "The kingdom of God does not come in a way you can see it coming.
People will not say, 'Look, here it is!' or 'Look, there it is!' Because the kingdom of God is among you."
Then he said to his followers, "The time will come when you will long to see one of the days of the Son of Man, but you will not see it.
People will tell you, 'Look, there he is!' or 'Look, here he is!' Do not go running after them.
For the Son of Man in his day will be like the lightning, which flashes and lights up the sky from one end to the other.
But first he must suffer many things and be rejected by the people of today.
Just as it was in the days of Noah, so it will be in the days of the Son of Man.
People were eating, drinking, marrying, and being given in marriage, up to the day Noah entered the ark. Then the flood came and destroyed them all.
It was the same in the days of Lot. People were eating and drinking, buying and selling, planting and building.
But on the day Lot left Sodom, fire and sulphur rained down from the sky and destroyed them all.
It will be just like that on the day the Son of Man is shown.
On that day, anyone on the roof, with their belongings in the house, must not go down to get them. Anyone in the field must not turn back.
Remember Lot's wife!
Whoever tries to keep their life will lose it, and whoever loses their life will keep it.
I tell you, on that night two people will be in one bed. One will be taken and the other left.
Two women will be grinding grain together. One will be taken and the other left."
They asked him, "Where, Lord?" He said, "Where there is a dead body, there the vultures will gather."
